title: Stability signature extraction + auto-pin recommender for A100/H100/L40S/MI300
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: when onboarding new model versions we publish a single performance profile per hardware SKU. That profile often hides transient instability modes (thermal throttling, PCIe contention, VM-level noisy neighbor effects) and per-batch memory headroom that cause version pinning decisions to be conservative or produce regressions in the field.

Goal: build a stability signature (time-series based meta-profile) for A100/H100/L40S/MI300 variants and a lightweight auto-pin recommender that consumes the signature + load signal to suggest: (a) whether a model version should be pinned to a specific SKU or bin, (b) safe batch/sequence headroom settings, and (c) compatible fallback variant mappings for graceful degradation.

This ticket covers the instrumentation, data schema, extraction algorithm, and a prototype recommender service that integrates with the model onboarding pipeline and profile publisher.
acceptance_criteria:
- Stability signatures exist for A100-40GB, A100-80GB, H100-80GB, L40S-64GB, MI300-256GB for the reference llama-2-70b and vicuna-13b test loads.
- Auto-pin recommender emits a JSON recommendation for each model+version in the onboarding flow (pin/no-pin, preferred bin, batch headroom, fallback mapping).
- Published profiles include stability metadata and a link to the raw time-series artifacts.
- Unit + integration tests for signature extractor and recommender with mocked perf traces.
- Documentation in Confluence: onboarding/stability-signature with runbook for re-running harness.
implementation_notes:
Design: offline harness runs 6 hour microbench windows across each SKU variant under three modes: baseline, background-noise (synthetic co-tenancy), and high-temperature (GPU fan constrained) to surface fragility. We compute per-window features: p99 latency drift, delta-throughput vs nominal, memory headroom distribution, KV cache eviction rate, PCIe retransmit spikes, and a heuristic thermal slope.

Signature format: flattened time-series summary: list of percentile vectors serialized as CSV link (artifact storage) + small JSON metadata (mean drift, fragility_score 0-1, recommended_headroom_pct). The publisher will attach fragility_score and version-stability-tag to the model variant entry in the catalog.

Recommender: rules-first prototype that maps fragility_score and workload SLO (latency_budget, batch_size, seq_len) to pin decisions. Example: fragility_score > 0.6 and latency_budget < 80ms -> recommend pin to dedicated H100 bin or fallback to a lower-capacity variant with quantized weights.

Integration: hook recommender into existing onboarding job (onboard-agent) so PRs that add a catalog model will surface the recommendation and a link to run the deeper 6h harness if needed.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for signature extractor with synthetic traces (noisy neighbor, thermal ramp, memory-pressure scenarios).
- End-to-end test: run 1h shortened harness across one A100 and one H100 instance in CI staging; assert recommender output matches expected mapping for synthetic patterns.
- Canary: publish signatures for one non-critical internal model and enable auto-pin only for dev tenants for 2 weeks.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge prototype and enable in onboarding-dev pipeline. 2) Run full 6h harnesses for target SKUs and publish signatures. 3) Monitor onboarding traffic and model-serving error rates for 2 weeks. 4) If stable, enable recommendations for all new onboarding flows and add a console flag to apply auto-pins automatically.
risks:
- MI300 perf counters are noisy in the current infra images; may need driver/kernel update (dependency on infra/devops).
- 6h harness multiplies GPU-hours cost for onboarding; we must budget and possibly optimize sampling windows.
- Rules-first recommender may miss complex interactions; will need telemetry to collect false positives/negatives and iterate toward ML-based model.
